subject: Post-call recap — streaming inference bottlenecks, p95 & next engineering steps
messages:
From: Elena Gomez <elena@streamlytics.io>
To: ava_chen@redwood.ai
Cc: Sales Ops <ops@streamlytics.io>
Date: 2026-05-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro call — streaming inference needs

Thanks for the call this morning, Ava. Really helpful to see where Redwood sits on serving and fallbacks. Quick recap from my side so we have alignment: 

Pain points we raised:
- Streaming UX jitter/end-of-stream pauses when we hit spikes (video -> embeddings -> enriched captions pipeline).
- P95 for token arrival to client currently ~380ms under load; goal is <=180ms for live captions.
- Concurrency: steady 1k concurrent live viewers per region, bursts to 3k for majors. Recent load test showed system dropped to 60% throughput at bursts.
- Cost: current provider is expensive on token-heavy streaming; we need predictable unit economics.

Current stack notes:
- Inference: combination of hosted LLM endpoints (vendor A) + local preprocessing cluster for embeddings.
- Caching: prefix cache implemented, but KV cache not surfaced to client layer.
- Auth: JWT short-lived tokens + S3 for artifacts.

Success criteria for PoC we discussed:
1) P95 <= 180ms for streaming token arrival for 512-token window (measured at client SDK).
2) Sustained 1k concurrency with bursts 3k without >5% error rate.
3) End-to-end cost improvement >= 25% compared to current monthly baseline.

Next steps from Streamlytics: we will share two representative prompt sets (short caption prompts + longer context expansion), a small sample of traffic traces, and a redacted network trace. I'll attach what I have today.

Thanks again — Elena
Elena Gomez
Head of Platform Engineering, Streamlytics

Attachment: network_trace_20260517.zip (1 file, 2.1 MB - stub)

From: ava_chen@redwood.ai
To: Elena Gomez <elena@streamlytics.io>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-18T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — streaming inference bottlenecks, p95 & next engineering steps

Elena — thanks for the clear summary and for the trace. I copied Karthik (solutions) and Rishi (infra/serving). Quick confirmation and what we’ll own for the PoC: 

Redwood commitments for initial PoC (proposed):
- Benchmark run: we will replicate a 1k steady / 3k burst concurrency test against a staged Redwood Dedicated pool and measure p95 at the SDK level.
- Streaming latency target tuning: aim to get observed token arrival p95 <= 180ms on your short prompt set by adjusting batching, KV cache policy, and prioritized scheduling.
- Cost estimate: provide an expected per-token cost delta and a monthlyized estimate for your traffic profile.
- Security: will provide an initial SOC2 evidence packet and a short doc on KMS integration.

Immediate asks for us to schedule the right infra test:
1) Can you send the two prompt sets and a 30-minute traffic trace (client timestamps + token counts)?
2) Which region(s) do you want us to test from? (we can run us-west and eu-west if helpful).
3) Any hard SLOs besides the p95 number (error budget, retention limits, or encryption-at-rest/ingress requirements)?

I’ll get the POC plan doc and a proposed test window in a follow-up. Attaching a short PoC outline now: proposed_poc_plan_streamlytics_v1.pdf (stub).

— Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0193

Attachment: proposed_poc_plan_streamlytics_v1.pdf (PDF stub)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: ava_chen@redwood.ai, Elena Gomez <elena@streamlytics.io>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-19T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — streaming inference bottlenecks, p95 & next engineering steps

Elena — quick technical note from my side: appreciate the trace. Two things I want to validate before we run the benchmark so we set expectations correctly: 

1) Client measurement point: is your p95 measurement taken at the SDK receiving token bytes or at the server-side emission event? We want the same client-side hook to align on numbers.

2) Tokenization/sequence length: your caption prompts look short (~40–80 tokens) but you mentioned context expansion. For test planning, please provide: typical prompt tokens, average expansion tokens, and max context window used during live runs. These numbers materially change batching and KV cache behavior.

Proposed short test: 10-minute warmup -> 30-minute steady at 1k clients -> 10-minute controlled 3k burst. We’ll run with: 25ms per-token scheduling micro-batches, KV cache enabled, and two model variants (quantized small model and baseline open large) to show tradeoffs. I’ll also add a tracing hook so you can see per-token timing and kernel-level stalls.

I’ll prepare an infra checklist (network, NAT concurrency, egress bandwidth) and share before the run.

— Karthik (Solutions Engineer)

Thanks Karthik — answers inline: 
1) Measurement: our p95 is measured at the client SDK receipt (we’ll package the SDK hook so you can run your measurement script).
2) Tokenization: typical prompt 45–70 tokens, expansion ~300 tokens for context; peaks up to ~900 tokens when we append historical context for re-syncs.

We prefer us-west for initial runs. Security: at minimum we need encryption-at-rest and per-tenant key separation; we can share specifics with your security team if needed.

Attaching two prompt files and a 30m trace (stripped PII). Also adding a short list of questions for the PoC: 
- Can you confirm whether KV cache will be warm outside of the single test run? (we want results that reflect real steady-state).
- Do you support prioritized streams so paid subscribers get lower-latency scheduling?

Looking forward to the PoC plan.

— Elena

Attachments: caption_prompts_v2.txt, expansion_prompts.txt, sample_trace_30m.json (stubs)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Elena Gomez <elena@streamlytics.io>, ava_chen@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-21T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — streaming inference bottlenecks, p95 & next engineering steps

Elena — Rishi here (infra). Appreciate the detail and the traces. Short answers and a couple asks so the PoC doesn't hit surprises: 

- KV cache: we can pre-warm the KV cache if you provide a representative corpus or a seed set; otherwise cold-start behavior will be worse. For fair steady-state numbers, provide the seed set or allow us to run a warmup period (recommended).
- Prioritized streams: yes, Redwood supports request prioritization policies at the routing layer; for the PoC we can set up two priority queues (gold/silver). We’ll show the latency separation on the dashboard.
- Network: please ensure outbound NAT concurrency on your side is at least 6k for the 3k burst test from a single region.

Action items I’ll take:
1) Prepare two benchmark runs (with and without cache warm) and the accompanying traces + dashboards.
2) Provide a short doc on key separation + KMS integration timeline.
3) Share an initial POC window: 2026-05-27 09:00–11:00 PT for the staged run (we can move if needed).

If that window works, Ava can put a calendar invite and we’ll lock infra for the run.

— Rishi Malhotra
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference
